text.p: Mediaset, the media group controlled by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, on Thursday denied a report that it was interested in taking over troubled information technology group Olivetti.

Rome daily Il Messaggero said Mediaset was attracted by the mobile phone consortium Omnitel in which Olivetti has a controlling stake. Mediaset has already said it is interested in bidding for a third Italian mobile telephone licence.
"Our strategy regarding cellular telephony has not changed, Mediaset said in a statement.
"Together with our partners British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, we have set up a working committee to take part in the auction for the third...operator."
The newspaper said investment bank Morgan Stanley had carried out a study into the viability of an Olivetti takeover.
"These are normal analyses that are submitted to us and which concern the major players in the telecommunications sector," the statement said.
A company spokesman declined to deny the report directly but industry figures said the Mediaset statement indicated the group was not interested in pursuing Olivetti.
